mainEntity.name: What temperature should a cold plunge be?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most people find 10°C to 15°C (50°F to 59°F) the sweet spot. Experienced plungers sometimes go colder, and our chillers can reach 37°F (2.8°C).

mainEntity.name: Can I use a cold plunge outdoors in a Canadian winter?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Cedar handles moisture and temperature swings well, and a cover helps. At 0°C (32°F) or below, either drain the tub or keep the chiller running so it doesn't freeze.
No. Fill with a garden hose and drain through the built-in drain. Chillers are self-contained and connect directly to the tub; their electrical connection must be made by a licensed electrician.
The Polar and Glacier come with either. 304 stainless steel is the premium, easy-clean option; HDPE is a durable, seamless liner at a lower price.

items.alt: Glacier cold plunge tub with stainless interior and Red Cedar skirt, The Toronto Sauna Co.
items.d: Our largest Dundalk plunge: 190 gallons with a 304 stainless steel or HDPE interior inside a warm Red Cedar skirt. Add a chiller for year-round cold, and drain it with a garden hose.

items.alt: Arctic cold plunge tub in knotty Red Cedar, The Toronto Sauna Co.
items.d: A welded HDPE shell wrapped in a Red Cedar skirt with stainless steel bands. Holds 132 gallons and ships fully assembled, ready for an optional chiller with ozone filter.

items.alt: Flow cold plunge with concealed chiller on a rooftop deck, The Toronto Sauna Co.
items.d: A stainless steel plunge wrapped in cedar, with the chiller hidden in a bay built into the shell. No hoses or equipment on show, just a clean finished look. Arrives fully assembled.

items.alt: Polar cold plunge tub in Eastern White Cedar, The Toronto Sauna Co.
items.d: A 190-gallon cold plunge in Eastern White Cedar, with your choice of a 304 stainless steel or white HDPE interior. Angled sides make it easy to step in and out, and a garden hose drain makes emptying simple.

items.alt: Baltic barrel cold plunge in Eastern White Cedar, The Toronto Sauna Co.
items.d: A classic barrel-style cold plunge in Eastern White Cedar, with an HDPE liner and stainless steel bands. Holds 132 gallons, ships assembled, and works with a chiller or plain ice.

blocks.html: Alternating a sauna session with a cold plunge is known as contrast therapy. Many people use it to support recovery, circulation and a clear head. Our plunges are handcrafted in Ontario from the same Canadian cedar as our saunas, so they look right side by side.
